findings.explanation: data/splunkbase-catalog.json lists Splunkbase 1747 as 'Splunk Add-on for Cisco WSA' (Splunk_TA_cisco-wsa), not the REST API Modular Input; the id is repeated in the references and detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: through REST API Modular Input (Splunkbase app ID 1747)
findings.suggested_fix: Look up the correct Splunkbase id (commonly 1546; verify) and fix every occurrence.

findings.explanation: The SPL alerts on fps=0, recording_gap_sec > 60 or stream_state=lost, and reports the latest gap rather than a count.
findings.suggested_fix: List all three conditions and the latest-gap output.

findings.explanation: 'Digest mode' is not a known Splunk alert option; batching is controlled by the Once versus For each result trigger setting.
findings.quote: scheduled alert with digest mode enabled so multiple degraded cameras batch into one notification
findings.suggested_fix: Say: set the alert trigger to Once so one notification covers all rows.

findings.explanation: Overlaps UC-15.3.4 and UC-15.3.11 (camera health) without stating how it differs.
findings.quote: Camera Feed Loss and Recording Gap Detection

findings.explanation: No real cause (motion-triggered recording producing intentional gaps, scheduled NVR maintenance) is named and count/span are not in the SPL.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: stats latest(recording_gap_sec) after the filter yields null for rows flagged only by fps=0 or stream_state=lost, so those cameras sort last in sort -gap.

summary: Concrete and mostly coherent stream-health UC, but it cites Splunkbase 1747 as the REST API Modular Input (the catalog lists a different add-on) and the description reports only one of three alert conditions.
